title: Example: mapping access to jobs and schools
text: Porto Alegre sample r5r 2.5.0 (OpenStreetMap extract, bus train GTFS feeds, grid 1,227 hexagonal cells population, jobs schools), downloaded temporary directory: cell point centre. bus feed sample trips late morning early evening weekdays, public transport routed 14:00 Monday, 30-minute window departures.
code: library(peabiru) library(sf) library(ggplot2)  poa <- file.path(tempdir(), "poa") dir.create(poa, showWarnings = FALSE) url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ipea/r5r/v2.5.0/r-package/inst/extdata/poa/" for (f in c("poa_osm.pbf", "poa_eptc.zip", "poa_trensurb.zip",             "poa_hexgrid.csv", "poa_points_of_interest.csv")) {   if (!file.exists(file.path(poa, f))) {     download.file(paste0(url, f), file.path(poa, f), mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)   } }  network <- build_network(poa) grid <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_hexgrid.csv")) head(grid) #>                id       lon       lat population schools jobs healthcare #> 1 89a901291abffff -51.15825 -30.05385          0       0 1214          0 #> 2 89a9012a3cfffff -51.21187 -30.10058        159       0    0          0 #> 3 89a901295b7ffff -51.16521 -30.07544       1008       0    3          1 #> 4 89a901284a3ffff -51.20535 -30.09005         92       0    0          0 #> 5 89a9012809bffff -51.19575 -30.07839        577       0    9          0 #> 6 89a901285cfffff -51.21108 -30.08124       1170       0  427          0 colSums(grid[, c("population", "schools", "jobs")], na.rm = TRUE) #> population    schools       jobs  #>     812935        194     337921 departure <- as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo")

title: Example: mapping access to jobs and schools
text: first look: travel time one place, Farroupilha Park, centre every cell. travel_time_matrix() leaves pairs take longer max_trip_duration. Within hour, public transport reaches four times many cells walking . map, cell drawn dot centre:
code: poi <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_points_of_interest.csv")) park <- poi[poi$id == "farroupilha_park", ]  from_park <- rbind(   data.frame(mode = "Walking", travel_time_matrix(     network, park, grid, mode = "WALK", max_trip_duration = 60)),   data.frame(mode = "Walking + public transport", travel_time_matrix(     network, park, grid, mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),     departure_datetime = departure, time_window = 30, max_trip_duration = 60)) ) sapply(split(from_park$travel_time_p50, from_park$mode),        function(t) c(cells = length(t), median_minutes = median(t))) #>                Walking Walking + public transport #> cells              268                       1100 #> median_minutes      41                         39 cells <- st_as_sf(grid, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) map <- merge(cells, from_park, by.x = "id", by.y = "to_id") ggplot(map) +   geom_sf(aes(colour = travel_time_p50), size = 1.2) +   scale_colour_gradient(low = "#7a3318", high = "#f5d3b6", name = "Minutes") +   facet_wrap(~mode) +   theme_void() +   theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))

title: Example: mapping access to jobs and schools
text: accessibility() adds , origin, opportunities every destination reached within cutoff ("step" decay function, default). Five cells job count; count zero, warning. Weighting cell people live gives average resident reaches: Public transport roughly triples : 21 thousand jobs 12 schools within half hour foot, 68 thousand jobs 31 schools buses train. map jobs reachable cell:
code: access <- rbind(   data.frame(mode = "Walking", accessibility(     network, grid, grid, opportunities_colnames = c("jobs", "schools"),     mode = "WALK", cutoffs = 30)),   data.frame(mode = "Walking + public transport", accessibility(     network, grid, grid, opportunities_colnames = c("jobs", "schools"),     mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"), departure_datetime = departure,     time_window = 30, cutoffs = 30)) ) #> Warning: `jobs` has 5 missing values, treated as 0. #> Warning: `jobs` has 5 missing values, treated as 0. head(access) #>      mode              id opportunity percentile cutoff accessibility #> 1 Walking 89a901291abffff        jobs         50     30         15978 #> 2 Walking 89a901291abffff     schools         50     30            12 #> 3 Walking 89a9012a3cfffff        jobs         50     30           641 #> 4 Walking 89a9012a3cfffff     schools         50     30             0 #> 5 Walking 89a901295b7ffff        jobs         50     30          1884 #> 6 Walking 89a901295b7ffff     schools         50     30            14 access <- merge(access, grid[, c("id", "population")], by = "id") sapply(split(access, list(access$opportunity, access$mode)), function(a)   round(weighted.mean(a$accessibility, a$population))) #>                       jobs.Walking                    schools.Walking  #>                              21343                                 12  #>    jobs.Walking + public transport schools.Walking + public transport  #>                              67725                                 31 jobs <- merge(cells, access[access$opportunity == "jobs", ], by = "id") ggplot(jobs) +   geom_sf(aes(colour = accessibility / 1000), size = 1.2) +   scale_colour_gradient(low = "#e3eadb", high = "#1f5139",                         name = "Thousand jobs") +   facet_wrap(~mode) +   theme_void() +   theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))

Several cutoffs . cutoffs = c(15, 30, 45) returns one row per cutoff, single routing pass. Percentiles. percentiles = c(25, 50, 75), accessibility good, typical bad departure window. maps home page draw results hexagons, site/figures/figures.R repository.

title: Accessibility
text: "step" function counts opportunities reached less cutoff. origin gets one row per opportunity column, percentile cutoff: "step", trips longer largest cutoff routed (max_trip_duration becomes max(cutoffs)), max_trip_duration may shorter largest cutoff function.
code: access <- accessibility(   network, points, points,   opportunities_colnames = c("jobs", "schools"),   mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),   departure_datetime = departure,   decay_function = "step",   cutoffs = c(15, 30),   percentiles = c(25, 75),   seed = 42,   n_threads = 2 ) head(access, 8) #> # A tibble: 8 × 5 #>   id              opportunity percentile cutoff accessibility #>   <chr>           <chr>            <int>  <int>         <dbl> #> 1 89a8100c00fffff jobs                25     15         12452 #> 2 89a8100c00fffff jobs                25     30         95249 #> 3 89a8100c00fffff jobs                75     15         12452 #> 4 89a8100c00fffff jobs                75     30         81835 #> 5 89a8100c00fffff schools             25     15             1 #> 6 89a8100c00fffff schools             25     30             4 #> 7 89a8100c00fffff schools             75     15             1 #> 8 89a8100c00fffff schools             75     30             4

title: Accessibility
text: functions weight every opportunity travel time. decay_value means different things: width ramp minutes "linear", standard deviation minutes "logistic", decay constant per second "fixed_exponential"; "exponential" uses cutoff half-life. "fixed_exponential" ignores cutoffs, cutoffs must NULL result cutoff column.
code: one <- function(fun, value = NULL, cutoffs = 20) {   a <- accessibility(     network, points[1:3, ], points,     opportunities_colnames = "jobs",     mode = "WALK",     decay_function = fun, decay_value = value, cutoffs = cutoffs,     n_threads = 2   )   setNames(round(a$accessibility), a$id) } rbind(   step = one("step"),   exponential = one("exponential"),   linear = one("linear", 10),   logistic = one("logistic", 5),   fixed_exponential = one("fixed_exponential", 0.001, cutoffs = NULL) ) #>                   89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c007ffff 89a8100c077ffff #> step                        16948           24325           31926 #> exponential                 42932           45737           48674 #> linear                      18205           22571           29017 #> logistic                    20363           25331           31449 #> fixed_exponential           23096           25598           28264

text: Income 2010 nothing newer exists resolution: Censo 2022 tables census tract IBGE’s server (listing 2026-11-12) population, households, literacy, colour race deaths, none income. residents 2010 , jobs 2019: public transport November 2026, people opportunities older. files downloaded directory (set PEABIRU_EXAMPLE_DATA keep somewhere else). Cutting extract needs osmium. Rio de Janeiro’s Belo Horizonte’s addresses always serve current file, later download another version network gives numbers; checksums (first 16 digits) identify files used . Mobility Database keeps São Paulo’s dated address.
code: library(peabiru) library(sf)  data_dir <- Sys.getenv("PEABIRU_EXAMPLE_DATA", "capitals-data") raw <- file.path(data_dir, "raw") dir.create(raw, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) options(timeout = 3600, HTTPUserAgent = "peabiru-docs-examples")  fetch <- function(url, name = basename(url)) {   dest <- file.path(raw, name)   if (!file.exists(dest)) download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)   dest } sudeste <- fetch("https://download.geofabrik.de/south-america/brazil/sudeste-261101.osm.pbf") aop <- function(file) {   fetch(paste0("https://github.com/ipeaGIT/aopdata/releases/download/v1.0.0/", file)) }  cities <- list(   spo = list(name = "São Paulo", code = "3550308", feed = "sptrans.zip", url = paste0(     "https://files.mobilitydatabase.org/mdb-8/mdb-8-202611120148/mdb-8-202611120148.zip")),   rio = list(name = "Rio de Janeiro", code = "3304557", feed = "smtr.zip",              url = "https://dados.mobilidade.rio/gtfs/schedule"),   bho = list(name = "Belo Horizonte", code = "3106200", feed = "bhtrans.zip",              url = "https://s3.amazonaws.com/mobilibus-uploads/gtfs/GTFSBHTRANS.zip") ) feeds <- sapply(cities, function(city) fetch(city$url, city$feed)) data.frame(MB = round(file.size(feeds) / 1e6, 1),            sha256 = substr(tools::sha256sum(feeds), 1, 16), row.names = basename(feeds)) #>               MB           sha256 #> sptrans.zip 14.3 70b6a2fccc120608 #> smtr.zip    25.3 a99f925460e7628b #> bhtrans.zip 52.2 15d3b184fe8e1e3a

title: Example: who reaches the jobs in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Belo Horizonte
text: street network city cut around municipality around stops feed (trains São Paulo’s feed run Jundiaí Mogi das Cruzes), 3 km spare. build_network() reads directory cut feed. routing, two checks cost nothing. build_network() refuses feed errors high priority, get_gtfs_errors() lists others; check_transit_availability() says much feed runs day chosen, Tuesday 17 November 2026 (Friday week holiday). None three feeds error. Belo Horizonte’s services run calendar one service per kind day system, weekday ones due Tuesday.
code: utm <- 31983   # SIRGAS 2000 / UTM zone 23S, in metres, for the three cities threads <- 4   # of the 10 of the laptop; the default is all of them  boundary_of <- function(code) {   url <- paste0("https://servicodados.ibge.gov.br/api/v3/malhas/municipios/", code,                 "?formato=application/vnd.geo+json&qualidade=maxima")   st_transform(st_make_valid(st_read(fetch(url, paste0(code, ".geojson")), quiet = TRUE)), utm) } stops_of <- function(zip) {   s <- read.csv(unz(zip, "stops.txt"), colClasses = "character")   s <- s[s$stop_lat != "" & s$stop_lon != "", ]   st_transform(st_as_sf(data.frame(lon = as.numeric(s$stop_lon), lat = as.numeric(s$stop_lat)),                         coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326), utm) }  networks <- list() for (k in names(cities)) {   dir <- file.path(data_dir, k, "network")   dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   file.copy(feeds[[k]], dir, overwrite = TRUE)   hull <- st_convex_hull(st_union(stops_of(feeds[[k]])))   area <- st_buffer(st_union(st_geometry(boundary_of(cities[[k]]$code)), hull), 3000)   polygon <- file.path(data_dir, k, "cut.geojson")   st_write(st_sf(geometry = st_transform(area, 4326)), polygon, delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)   pbf <- file.path(dir, paste0(k, ".osm.pbf"))   stopifnot(system2("osmium", c("extract", "--overwrite", "-p", polygon, sudeste, "-o", pbf)) == 0)   networks[[k]] <- build_network(dir, n_threads = threads)   cat(sprintf("%s: %.0f km2, %.1f MB\n", k, as.numeric(st_area(area)) / 1e6, file.size(pbf) / 1e6)) } #> spo: 4726 km2, 140.5 MB #> rio: 2097 km2, 27.6 MB #> bho: 696 km2, 6.4 MB networks$spo #> <peabiru_network> #>   data path: capitals-data/spo/network #>   streets:   561,300 vertices, 1,490,420 edges #>   transit:   1 feed(s) (sptrans), 22,270 stops, 2,269 patterns, 6 services, frequency-based trips #>   elevation: NONE networks$rio #> <peabiru_network> #>   data path: capitals-data/rio/network #>   streets:   204,000 vertices, 523,562 edges #>   transit:   1 feed(s) (SMTR-PCRJ), 7,694 stops, 961 patterns, 3 services, frequency-based trips #>   elevation: NONE networks$bho #> <peabiru_network> #>   data path: capitals-data/bho/network #>   streets:   107,414 vertices, 286,400 edges #>   transit:   1 feed(s) (bhtrans), 9,924 stops, 1,118 patterns, 14 services #>   elevation: NONE day <- as.Date("2026-11-17") do.call(rbind, lapply(names(cities), function(k) {   cbind(city = k, gtfs_errors = nrow(get_gtfs_errors(networks[[k]])),         check_transit_availability(networks[[k]], dates = day)) })) #>   city gtfs_errors       date total_services active_services pct_active #> 1  spo           0 2026-11-17              6               3  0.5000000 #> 2  rio           0 2026-11-17              3               1  0.3333333 #> 3  bho           0 2026-11-17             14               2  0.1428571

text: Ipea’s grid , cell, residents (P001), average household income per person (R001), income decile cell among residents city (R003, 1 poorest tenth), formal jobs (T001), public schools (E001) public health facilities (S001). cell routed , , centre.
code: cells_of <- function(k) {   grid <- st_read(aop(sprintf("hex_grid_%s.gpkg", k)), quiet = TRUE)[, "id_hex"]   people <- read.csv(aop(sprintf("population_2010_%s.csv", k)))   land <- read.csv(aop(sprintf("landuse_2019_%s.csv", k)))   cells <- merge(grid, people[, c("id_hex", "P001", "R001", "R003")], by = "id_hex")   cells <- merge(cells, land[, c("id_hex", "T001", "E001", "S001")], by = "id_hex")   names(cells)[1:7] <- c("id", "population", "income", "decile", "jobs", "schools", "health")   centre <- st_coordinates(st_transform(st_centroid(st_transform(st_geometry(cells), utm)), 4326))   cells$lon <- round(centre[, 1], 6)   cells$lat <- round(centre[, 2], 6)   cells } grids <- lapply(setNames(names(cities), names(cities)), cells_of) t(sapply(grids, function(g) c(cells = nrow(g), inhabited = sum(g$population > 0),                               residents = sum(g$population), jobs = sum(g$jobs),                               schools = sum(g$schools), health = sum(g$health)))) #>     cells inhabited residents    jobs schools health #> spo 15059      9704  11163678 3461972    2632    885 #> rio 11916      6392   6141600 1580698    1811    389 #> bho  3049      2548   2409892  720512     544    341

code: departure <- as.POSIXct("2026-11-17 07:00:00", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo")  access_of <- function(k) {   cells <- st_drop_geometry(grids[[k]])   origins <- cells[cells$population > 0, ]   destinations <- cells[cells$jobs + cells$schools + cells$health > 0, ]   a <- accessibility(     networks[[k]], origins, destinations,     opportunities_colnames = c("jobs", "schools", "health"),     mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"), departure_datetime = departure, time_window = 60,     percentiles = 50, cutoffs = c(30, 60), max_trip_duration = 60, seed = 42,     n_threads = threads, progress = FALSE)   cat(sprintf("%s: %d origins x %d destinations\n", k, nrow(origins), nrow(destinations)))   # one row per cell, one column per opportunity and cutoff: jobs_60, ...   a$what <- paste(a$opportunity, a$cutoff, sep = "_")   wide <- reshape(as.data.frame(a[, c("id", "what", "accessibility")]), idvar = "id",                   timevar = "what", direction = "wide")   names(wide) <- sub("accessibility.", "", names(wide), fixed = TRUE)   merge(origins, wide, by = "id") } access <- lapply(setNames(names(cities), names(cities)), access_of) #> spo: 9704 origins x 8482 destinations #> rio: 6392 origins x 4991 destinations #> ! Less than 20% of the transit services in the GTFS are running on the selected departure date. #> bho: 2548 origins x 2330 destinations weighted_median <- function(x, w) {   o <- order(x)   x[o][which(cumsum(w[o]) >= sum(w) / 2)[1]] } shares <- t(sapply(names(cities), function(k) {   a <- access[[k]]   share <- a$jobs_60 / sum(grids[[k]]$jobs)   c(mean = weighted.mean(share, a$population), median = weighted_median(share, a$population),     none = weighted.mean(a$jobs_60 == 0, a$population)) })) round(100 * shares, 1) #>     mean median none #> spo 14.7    8.1    0 #> rio 25.4   20.9    0 #> bho 58.7   71.2    0

{     con <- unz(src, name, open = "rb")     to <- file(file.path(tmp, name), "wb")     header <- readLines(con, n = 1)     writeLines(header, to)     k <- keep[[name]]     col <- if (is.null(k)) NA text: build_network() reads .pbf GTFS feeds directory keeps result memory. street network one edge per direction every street segment, modes allowed , car speed , cyclists, level traffic stress; public transport grouped patterns (trips stop stops order). stop joined nearest walkable street, two walking tables computed : transfers nearby stops (1 km) walking distances every stop (2 km), used reach destinations. step fixed rules details matter ties: order ways, feeds stops read, two equal paths kept, lengths speeds rounded. inputs therefore give network, results, whatever number threads.

title: How it works
text: search public transport RAPTOR (Round-bAsed Public Transit Optimized Router): round k finds earliest arrival every stop k vehicles, max_rides simply number rounds. Running minute window last minute back first lets minute start results later one (“range RAPTOR”), much cheaper independent searches. Frequency-based trips fixed departure times. every minute repeated draws_per_minute times random offsets, drawn Mersenne Twister seeded seed origin’s coordinates, seed gives numbers every run number threads.

what: Travel times on the street network
title: Get started with peabiru
text: travel_time_matrix() one street mode gives travel time whole minutes every origin every destination; pairs reached within max_trip_duration (120 minutes default) left . results tibbles. options(peabiru.output = "data.frame") makes every function return base data frames instead, options(peabiru.output = "data.table") data.tables; rows, columns values whatever class. article “peabiru sf tidyverse” goes points maps sf, dplyr ggplot2. Walking walk_speed (3.6 km/h default). Cycling bike_speed streets whose level traffic stress max_lts; elsewhere cyclist walks bike. Driving uses street’s speed, turn costs turn restrictions.
code: walk <- travel_time_matrix(network, points, points, mode = "WALK",                            n_threads = 2) head(walk) #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>   from_id         to_id           travel_time_p50 #>   <chr>           <chr>                     <int> #> 1 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c00fffff               0 #> 2 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c007ffff               7 #> 3 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c077ffff              10 #> 4 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c03bffff               8 #> 5 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c033ffff              13 #> 6 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c0afffff              23  bike <- travel_time_matrix(network, points, points, mode = "BICYCLE",                            n_threads = 2) car <- travel_time_matrix(network, points, points, mode = "CAR",                           n_threads = 2) sapply(list(walk = walk, bike = bike, car = car),        function(m) mean(m$travel_time_p50)) #>      walk      bike       car  #> 19.696845 11.817558  7.462277

title: Get started with peabiru
text: mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT") trip combines walking public transport. departure time needed, result summarises trips leave minute time_window percentiles. feed frequency-based, departures simulated random draws: give seed make reproducible. Walking way one options considered, adding public transport never makes trip longer; small network shortens many longer ones:

title: Example: access to schools and health care in Recife and Caruaru
text: files downloaded directory (set PEABIRU_EXAMPLE_DATA keep somewhere else). Cutting extract needs osmium (brew install osmium-tool, apt install osmium-tool, conda-forge).
code: library(peabiru) library(sf)  data_dir <- Sys.getenv("PEABIRU_EXAMPLE_DATA", "pe-data") raw <- file.path(data_dir, "raw") dir.create(raw, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) options(timeout = 3600)   # the extract is 445 MB  fetch <- function(url, name = basename(url)) {   dest <- file.path(raw, name)   if (!file.exists(dest)) download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)   dest } nordeste <- fetch("https://download.geofabrik.de/south-america/brazil/nordeste-261101.osm.pbf") tracts_file <- fetch(paste0("https://ftp.ibge.gov.br/Censos/Censo_Demografico_2022/",                             "Agregados_por_Setores_Censitarios/malha_com_atributos/",                             "setores/gpkg/UF/PE/PE_setores_CD2022.gpkg")) schools_file <- fetch("https://www.ipea.gov.br/geobr/data_gpkg/schools/2023/schools_2023.gpkg") cnes_file <- fetch(paste0("https://s3.sa-east-1.amazonaws.com/ckan.saude.gov.br/CNES/",                           "cnes_estabelecimentos_csv.zip"))  cities <- data.frame(key = c("recife", "caruaru"),                      code = c("2611606", "2604106"),   # IBGE codes                      buffer = c(10000, 5000))          # metres utm <- 31985   # SIRGAS 2000 / UTM zone 25S, in metres, for both cities

what: Streets: the municipality and a buffer
title: Example: access to schools and health care in Recife and Caruaru
text: boundary municipality comes IBGE’s API. Buffered metres, polygon osmium extract cuts regional extract ; cut goes directory , build_network() reads.
code: boundary_of <- function(code) {   url <- paste0("https://servicodados.ibge.gov.br/api/v3/malhas/municipios/", code,                 "?formato=application/vnd.geo+json&qualidade=maxima")   b <- st_read(fetch(url, paste0(code, ".geojson")), quiet = TRUE)   st_transform(st_make_valid(b), utm) }  cut_streets <- function(key, boundary, buffer) {   dir <- file.path(data_dir, key, "network")   dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   polygon <- file.path(data_dir, key, "cut.geojson")   st_write(st_transform(st_buffer(boundary, buffer), 4326), polygon,            delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)   pbf <- file.path(dir, paste0(key, ".osm.pbf"))   status <- system2("osmium", c("extract", "--overwrite", "-p", polygon, nordeste, "-o", pbf))   stopifnot(status == 0)   dir }  boundaries <- lapply(setNames(cities$code, cities$key), boundary_of) networks <- list() for (i in seq_len(nrow(cities))) {   k <- cities$key[i]   dir <- cut_streets(k, boundaries[[k]], cities$buffer[i])   networks[[k]] <- build_network(dir)   cat(sprintf("%-8s %5.1f MB\n", k, file.size(file.path(dir, paste0(k, ".osm.pbf"))) / 1e6)) } #> recife    16.0 MB #> caruaru    1.9 MB networks$recife #> <peabiru_network> #>   data path: pe-data/recife/network #>   streets:   104,331 vertices, 275,968 edges #>   transit:   none (no GTFS feed) #>   elevation: NONE networks$caruaru #> <peabiru_network> #>   data path: pe-data/caruaru/network #>   streets:   28,445 vertices, 78,318 edges #>   transit:   none (no GTFS feed) #>   elevation: NONE

what: Where people live: a hexagonal grid with the census
title: Example: access to schools and health care in Recife and Caruaru
text: census counts people tract, tracts vary city block hundreds square kilometres. regular grid makes cities comparable: hexagons 500 m apart, numbered row row south-west, whole municipality. cell gets population tracts covers, proportion area covers . Censo 2022 counts 1,488,924 people Recife 378,048 Caruaru; grid keeps 127 Recife, tracts reach slightly outside IBGE’s municipal boundary. Caruaru’s grid four times many cells Recife’s quarter people: municipality rural, large rural tracts spread people cell.
code: hex_grid <- function(area, spacing = 500) {   b <- st_bbox(area)   h <- spacing * sqrt(3) / 2   centres <- expand.grid(i = -1:(ceiling((b[["xmax"]] - b[["xmin"]]) / spacing) + 1),                          j = -1:(ceiling((b[["ymax"]] - b[["ymin"]]) / h) + 1))   centres$x <- b[["xmin"]] + centres$i * spacing + (centres$j %% 2) * spacing / 2   centres$y <- b[["ymin"]] + centres$j * h   k <- (30 + 60 * 0:6) * pi / 180   # pointy side up   r <- spacing / sqrt(3)   cells <- st_sfc(lapply(seq_len(nrow(centres)), function(n)     st_polygon(list(cbind(centres$x[n] + r * cos(k), centres$y[n] + r * sin(k))))),     crs = st_crs(area))   cells <- cells[lengths(st_intersects(cells, area)) > 0]   st_sf(id = seq_along(cells), geometry = cells) }  population_grid <- function(code, boundary) {   tracts <- st_read(tracts_file, quiet = TRUE, query = paste0(     "SELECT v0001, geom FROM PE_setores_CD2022 WHERE CD_MUN = '", code, "'"))   tracts <- st_transform(st_make_valid(tracts), utm)   tracts$tract_area <- as.numeric(st_area(tracts))   cells <- hex_grid(boundary)   parts <- suppressWarnings(st_intersection(cells, tracts))   parts$people <- parts$v0001 * as.numeric(st_area(parts)) / parts$tract_area   people <- tapply(parts$people, parts$id, sum)   cells$population <- 0   cells$population[match(as.integer(names(people)), cells$id)] <- people   centres <- st_coordinates(st_transform(st_centroid(st_geometry(cells)), 4326))   cells$lon <- round(centres[, 1], 6)   cells$lat <- round(centres[, 2], 6)   cells$id <- as.character(cells$id)   cells[cells$population > 0, ] }  grids <- list() for (i in seq_len(nrow(cities))) {   k <- cities$key[i]   grids[[k]] <- population_grid(cities$code[i], boundaries[[k]])   cat(sprintf("%-8s %5d cells, %s people\n", k, nrow(grids[[k]]),               format(round(sum(grids[[k]]$population)), big.mark = ","))) } #> recife    1107 cells, 1,488,797 people #> caruaru   4489 cells, 378,048 people

title: Example: access to schools and health care in Recife and Caruaru
text: Schools: INEP’s catalogue public (municipal, state federal) open restriction, coordinates. Health units: CNES establishments types 1 (posto de saúde) 2 (centro de saúde / unidade básica), primary health care units SUS, active coordinates. taken whole area cut OpenStreetMap, nearest unit can across municipal border, often people living near . things know registers, seen preparing : public schools operation, 22 486 Recife 15 168 Caruaru coordinates catalogue placed; left . 167 active primary care units registered Recife, six coordinates outside municipality: four hundred metres across border, one 24 km away, Ilha de Itamaracá, one 20 km away, Moreno. Caruaru, two 75 , one 5 km . Taking units rather registered keeps far ones figures (fall outside cut area), units missing neighbourhoods. Schools health units sit close streets extract: median distance nearest street 7 16 m, single school city 300 m one (418 m Recife, 574 m Caruaru), well within 1.6 km peabiru links point street network.
code: cut_area <- function(k) st_transform(st_read(file.path(data_dir, k, "cut.geojson"),                                              quiet = TRUE), 4674)  schools_in <- function(area) {   s <- st_read(schools_file, quiet = TRUE, wkt_filter = st_as_text(st_as_sfc(st_bbox(area))),                query = paste("SELECT code_school, name_school, name_muni, geom",                              "FROM schools_2023 WHERE admin_category = 'Pública'",                              "AND service_restriction = 'ESCOLA EM FUNCIONAMENTO",                              "E SEM RESTRIÇÃO DE ATENDIMENTO'"))   s <- s[!st_is_empty(s), ]   s <- s[lengths(st_intersects(s, area)) > 0, ]   xy <- st_coordinates(s)   data.frame(id = as.character(s$code_school), name = s$name_school,              municipality = s$name_muni, lon = xy[, 1], lat = xy[, 2]) }  cnes <- read.csv2(unz(cnes_file, "cnes_estabelecimentos.csv"), fileEncoding = "latin1",                   colClasses = "character", na.strings = character()) cnes <- cnes[cnes$CO_UF == "26" & cnes$TP_UNIDADE %in% c("1", "2") &                cnes$CO_MOTIVO_DESAB == "" & cnes$NU_LATITUDE != "", ] health_in <- function(area) {   h <- data.frame(id = cnes$CO_CNES, name = cnes$NO_FANTASIA,                   municipality_code = cnes$CO_IBGE,                   lon = as.numeric(cnes$NU_LONGITUDE), lat = as.numeric(cnes$NU_LATITUDE))   inside <- lengths(st_intersects(st_as_sf(h, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4674), area)) > 0   h[inside, ] }  schools <- lapply(setNames(cities$key, cities$key), function(k) schools_in(cut_area(k))) health <- lapply(setNames(cities$key, cities$key), function(k) health_in(cut_area(k))) sapply(cities$key, function(k) c(schools = nrow(schools[[k]]), health_units = nrow(health[[k]]))) #>              recife caruaru #> schools         937     216 #> health_units    511     102

code: dem_of <- function(k, arcsec = 3) {   prepare_dem(k, arcsec = arcsec)   tag <- if (arcsec == 1) "" else "90"   terra::rast(file.path(data_dir, k, paste0("network-dem", tag), paste0(k, "_dem", tag, ".tif"))) } r <- dem_of("rmr") v <- terra::values(r, mat = FALSE) c(res_arcsec = terra::res(r)[1] * 3600, voids = sum(is.na(v) | v < -1000),   sea_share = round(mean(v == 0), 3), below_0_share = round(mean(v < 0), 4),   min_m = round(min(v), 1), max_m = round(max(v), 1)) #>    res_arcsec         voids     sea_share below_0_share         min_m  #>        3.0000        0.0000        0.1950        0.0014      -17.1000  #>         max_m  #>      446.4000 # street samples every 10 m at the nearest pixel streets_z <- function(k, arcsec = 3, bridges = FALSE) {   lines <- suppressWarnings(st_read(file.path(data_dir, k, "network", paste0(k, ".osm.pbf")),                                     "lines", quiet = TRUE))   lines <- lines[!is.na(lines$highway), ]   is_bridge <- grepl('"bridge"=>"(yes|viaduct)"', lines$other_tags)   lines <- st_transform(lines[if (bridges) is_bridge else !is_bridge, ], 31985)   lines <- lines[as.numeric(st_length(lines)) >= 20, ]   pts <- st_line_sample(lines, density = 1 / 10, type = "regular")   n <- vapply(pts, function(p) if (st_is_empty(p)) 0L else nrow(st_coordinates(p)), 1L)   ll <- sf_project(st_crs(31985), st_crs(4326), st_coordinates(pts)[, 1:2])   data.frame(way = rep(lines$osm_id, n), lon = ll[, 1], lat = ll[, 2],              z = terra::extract(dem_of(k, arcsec), ll, method = "simple")[, 1]) } in_boa_viagem <- function(lon, lat) lon > -34.925 & lon < -34.885 & lat > -8.145 & lat < -8.09  sapply(c("GLO-30" = 1, "GLO-90" = 3), function(arcsec) {   s <- streets_z("recife", arcsec)   bv <- s[in_boa_viagem(s$lon, s$lat), ]   same_way <- bv$way[-1] == bv$way[-nrow(bv)]   c(samples = nrow(bv), round(quantile(bv$z, c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99)), 1),     steps_over_2m = round(mean(abs(diff(bv$z))[same_way] > 2), 3)) }) #>                  GLO-30    GLO-90 #> samples       23528.000 23528.000 #> 10%               2.500     3.100 #> 50%               4.500     4.700 #> 90%               9.200     9.100 #> 99%              13.400    12.900 #> steps_over_2m     0.075     0.025 b <- streets_z("rmr", bridges = TRUE) sag <- sapply(split(b$z, b$way), function(z) {   if (length(z) < 3) NA else mean(z[c(1, length(z))]) - min(z[-c(1, length(z))]) }) sag <- sag[!is.na(sag)] c(bridges = length(sag), dip_over_2m = round(mean(sag > 2), 3),   dip_over_5m = round(mean(sag > 5), 3), worst_m = round(max(sag), 1)) #>     bridges dip_over_2m dip_over_5m     worst_m  #>     358.000       0.209       0.036       8.700

code: grid_of <- function(k) {   g <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, k, "cells.csv"), colClasses = c(id = "character"))   g[g$population > 0, ] } units_of <- function(k, what) {   read.csv(file.path(data_dir, k, paste0(what, ".csv")), colClasses = c(id = "character")) } # the time from each cell to the nearest school and health unit, and which one nearest <- function(k, elevation, mode, max_lts = 2) {   out <- grid_of(k)   for (what in c("schools", "health")) {     m <- travel_time_matrix(network(k, elevation), out, units_of(k, what), mode = mode,                             max_lts = max_lts, max_trip_duration = 60)     m <- m[order(m$from_id, m$travel_time_p50, m$to_id), ]     m <- m[!duplicated(m$from_id), ]     i <- match(out$id, m$from_id)     out[[what]] <- m$travel_time_p50[i]        # NA: none within the hour     out[[paste0(what, "_id")]] <- m$to_id[i]   }   out } share <- function(t, what, minutes = 15) {   round(100 * sum(t$population[!is.na(t[[what]]) & t[[what]] <= minutes]) / sum(t$population), 1) }  # what a raster adds to the walk to the nearest health unit, in minutes # averaged over the residents, and the share of them who lose 2 or more added <- function(k, elevation, inside = function(lon, lat) TRUE) {   flat <- nearest(k, "NONE", "WALK")   hill <- nearest(k, elevation, "WALK")   d <- hill$health - flat$health   ok <- !is.na(d) & inside(flat$lon, flat$lat)   c(residents = round(sum(flat$population[inside(flat$lon, flat$lat)])),     minutes_added = round(weighted.mean(d[ok], flat$population[ok]), 2),     lose_2_or_more = round(100 * sum(flat$population[ok & d >= 1.5]) / sum(flat$population[ok]), 1)) } rbind("Boa Viagem, GLO-30" = added("recife", "TOBLER30", in_boa_viagem),       "Boa Viagem, GLO-90" = added("recife", "TOBLER", in_boa_viagem),       "Recife, GLO-30" = added("recife", "TOBLER30"),       "Recife, GLO-90" = added("recife", "TOBLER"),       "Salvador, GLO-30" = added("salvador", "TOBLER30"),       "Salvador, GLO-90" = added("salvador", "TOBLER"),       "Petrolina, GLO-30" = added("petrolina", "TOBLER30"),       "Petrolina, GLO-90" = added("petrolina", "TOBLER")) #>                    residents minutes_added lose_2_or_more #> Boa Viagem, GLO-30    206103          1.04           26.1 #> Boa Viagem, GLO-90    206103          0.15            1.0 #> Recife, GLO-30       1488797          1.05           26.2 #> Recife, GLO-90       1488797          0.42            5.5 #> Salvador, GLO-30     2418518          2.28           60.2 #> Salvador, GLO-90     2418518          1.26           31.8 #> Petrolina, GLO-30     409608          0.30            2.2 #> Petrolina, GLO-90     409608          0.16            0.2

code: munis <- st_read(file.path(data_dir, "rmr", "boundary.geojson"), quiet = TRUE) unit_muni <- function(units) {   p <- st_as_sf(units, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4674)   hit <- st_intersects(st_transform(p, st_crs(munis)), munis)   setNames(vapply(hit, function(i) if (length(i)) munis$code[i[1]] else "outside", ""), units$id) } # the residents of each cell, by the municipality of their census tract by_muni <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "rmr", "cells_muni.csv"),                     colClasses = c(id = "character", code = "character")) by_muni <- by_muni[by_muni$id %in% grid_of("rmr")$id, ] across <- function(what) {   units <- units_of("rmr", what)   m <- travel_time_matrix(network("rmr", "TOBLER"), grid_of("rmr"), units, mode = "WALK",                           max_trip_duration = 60)   # the time from each cell to the nearest unit of each municipality   best <- tapply(m$travel_time_p50, list(m$from_id, unit_muni(units)[m$to_id]), min)   rows <- match(by_muni$id, rownames(best))   own <- best[cbind(rows, match(by_muni$code, colnames(best)))]   other <- vapply(seq_along(rows), function(i) {     if (is.na(rows[i])) return(NA_real_)     v <- best[rows[i], colnames(best) != by_muni$code[i]]     if (all(is.na(v))) NA_real_ else min(v, na.rm = TRUE)   }, 0)   nearer <- !is.na(other) & (is.na(own) | other < own)   people <- tapply(by_muni$population * nearer, by_muni$code, sum)   total <- tapply(by_muni$population, by_muni$code, sum)   list(region = c(people = round(sum(people)), share = round(100 * sum(people) / sum(total), 1),                   tied = round(sum(by_muni$population[!is.na(other) & !is.na(own) & other == own]))),        top = round(100 * sort(people / total, decreasing = TRUE)[1:4], 1)) } codes <- c("2610707" = "Paulista", "2609600" = "Olinda", "2603454" = "Camaragibe",            "2611606" = "Recife", "2607752" = "Itapissuma", "2606804" = "Igarassu",            "2607901" = "Jaboatão dos Guararapes", "2613701" = "São Lourenço da Mata") for (what in c("schools", "health")) {   x <- across(what)   names(x$top) <- codes[names(x$top)]   print(x) } #> $region #>   people    share     tied  #> 108906.0      2.9  13487.0  #>  #> $top #>   Paulista Itapissuma   Igarassu Camaragibe  #>       11.6        4.5        3.3        2.9  #>  #> $region #> people  share   tied  #> 147740      4  14642  #>  #> $top #>   Paulista     Olinda Camaragibe     Recife  #>        9.3        8.7        5.1        3.7 added("rmr", "TOBLER") #>      residents  minutes_added lose_2_or_more  #>     3730664.00           0.49           8.10

text: São Paulo sample ships package feed described frequencies (“bus every 8 minutes”) rather timetables. routes peabiru draws random schedules consistent frequencies, 5 per departure minute default, travel times window departures form distribution. seed makes draws reproducible. destinations closest origin walked , every departure takes time. away, bus metro saves time, spread 5th 95th percentiles price knowing comes:
code: spo <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru") network <- build_network(spo) points <- read.csv(file.path(spo, "spo_points.csv")) departure <- as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo")  ttm <- travel_time_matrix(   network, points[1, ], points[-1, ],   mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),   departure_datetime = departure,   time_window = 60,   percentiles = c(5, 25, 50, 75, 95),   seed = 42 ) ttm <- ttm[order(ttm$travel_time_p50, ttm$travel_time_p95), ] head(ttm) #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>   from_id  to_id travel_time_p05 travel_time_p25 travel_time_p50 travel_time_p75 #>   <chr>    <chr>           <int>           <int>           <int>           <int> #> 1 89a8100… 89a8…               7               7               7               7 #> 2 89a8100… 89a8…               8               8               8               8 #> 3 89a8100… 89a8…              10              10              10              10 #> 4 89a8100… 89a8…              13              13              13              13 #> 5 89a8100… 89a8…              14              14              14              14 #> 6 89a8100… 89a8…              17              17              17              17 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: travel_time_p95 <int> ttm$destination <- factor(ttm$to_id, levels = rev(ttm$to_id)) ggplot(ttm, aes(y = destination)) +   geom_linerange(aes(xmin = travel_time_p05, xmax = travel_time_p95),                  colour = "#c98a1d", linewidth = 1) +   geom_linerange(aes(xmin = travel_time_p25, xmax = travel_time_p75),                  colour = "#b4532a", linewidth = 3) +   geom_point(aes(x = travel_time_p50), shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2) +   labs(x = "Travel time (minutes)", y = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

text: t travel time c cutoff: "step": weight 1 cutoff, 0 (cumulative opportunities). Trips longer largest cutoff routed (max_trip_duration becomes max(cutoffs)). "exponential": 2^(-t / c), half weight cutoff; 0 two hours . "fixed_exponential": exp(-decay_value * t) t seconds, without cutoffs; 0 two hours . "linear": 1 decay_value / 2 minutes cutoff, 0 decay_value / 2 minutes , falling linearly . "logistic": logistic curve median cutoff standard deviation decay_value minutes, scaled 1 t = 0. weights computed table-based exponential (translation FastMath.exp() Apache Commons Math), sums , last bit, every machine. Except "step", max_trip_duration may shorter largest cutoff. fare_structure, public transport routed fares travel_time_matrix() (see section "Departures Monte Carlo draws").

title: Choose where to open new facilities — locate_facilities
text: "max_cover", maximal covering (Church ReVelle, 1974): n_facilities new facilities, cover demand within cutoff minutes. "set_cover", location set covering (Toregas et al., 1971): fewest new facilities leave every demand point within cutoff minutes one (every point site can cover; demand others reported summary$unservable_demand). "p_median" (Hakimi, 1964): n_facilities new facilities smallest demand-weighted sum travel times nearest facility. "p_center" (Hakimi, 1964): n_facilities new facilities smallest travel time demand point farthest nearest facility. existing facilities already open count first: demand leave uncovered, travel time leave, drives choice new sites. never closed moved.

title: Choose where to open new facilities — locate_facilities
text: heuristics, integer programming solver: greedy construction (site one improves objective , given ones ) followed, swap, vertex substitution (Teitz Bart, 1968): open new site swapped closed candidate improves objective, best swap step. "set_cover" greedy choice site covering points yet covered, improvement drops sites others make redundant; "p_center" greedy swaps compare largest travel time , ties, weighted sum. solution good reproducible, proven optimal. maximal covering greedy solution covers least 63% (1 - 1/e) covered demand yet covered (Nemhauser, Wolsey Fisher, 1978). Ties go candidate listed first, result depend n_threads. "set_cover" "p_center" demand point weight 0 demand, others count whatever weight. "p_median" "p_center" demand point reaches open facility (within max_trip_duration) charged unreachable_time minutes, one site reaches left reported.
